# The Absys harness

*Phase 4, wave 1, against `spec-1.0`. Written by the Absys harness author
(an agent, `harness-absys`), from `harnesses/README.md` (the common
contract), `systems/absys/README.md` and the pinned sources in the image
(`/opt/src/absys`, `/opt/src/absys-measure`). It changes no frozen file.
Where the contract could not be implemented as written, the reading taken
is in [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md).*

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `run` | the harness: `run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR` |
| `check` | `check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM`: syntax and static errors, executing nothing |
| `absys_harness.py` | the code of both |
| `README.md` | this file: how the harness works, and **the contract a program for Absys must meet** |
| [`S-mechanisms.md`](S-mechanisms.md) | the S mechanisms of each configuration (none) |
| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | what could not be implemented as written, and the reading implemented |
| [`qualification/`](qualification) | made-up programs, the script that reruns every test, its output and its records |

## 1. Running it

Inside the pinned image, from the repository root mounted at `/work`:

    container run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --volume "$PWD":/work --workdir /work \
        cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0 \
        harnesses/absys/run absys P01 P01a behaviour PROGRAM results/absys/absys/P01/raw

and for P12, P13 and P16 add `--memory 16g` (or more) after `container run`
(see **Memory** below).

The harness is Python 3.11, standard library only (`/usr/bin/python3` of
the image). It runs the pinned builds in `/usr/local/bin` and installs
nothing. Exit status, as the common contract says: 0 when a valid record
was written, whatever the outcome; 2 for a usage error, with no record; 3
when the record does not validate, kept as `<run_id>.INVALID.json`.

Environment variables it reads, none of which changes what the system
computes:

| variable | what |
|---|---|
| `CP_IMAGE_DIGEST` | the image digest, for `system_build.image`; the launcher may pass it (the harness cannot read it from inside). Otherwise `null` |
| `ABSYS_HARNESS_PURPOSE` | `primary` (default), `variant` (the verifier's) or `qualification` |
| `ABSYS_HARNESS_VARIANT` | the hidden variant's id, with `variant` |
| `ABSYS_HARNESS_STAGES` | another stages file; used only by the qualification, for its made-up problems |
| `ABSYS_HARNESS_POSING=reposed` | qualification only: every stage after the first is posed by reposing, so that the two ways can be compared |

**Memory.** The machine keeps every event of a run in memory, whether or
not the trace is shown (`Ctx.events`): about 85 bytes a step, measured in
the image. Under the container's default of 1 GiB, a computation is killed
by the kernel near 10⁷ steps, well before a budget of 10⁸ (P12, P13, P16).
The harness records that as *error*, with the signal (qualification,
X21a). **Run P12, P13 and P16 with `container run --memory 16g`** or more
(10⁸ steps is about 8.5 GB in one assertion).

## 2. Configurations

| configuration | flags the harness passes | alternatives held as |
|---|---|---|
| `absys` | none | `all-live` |
| `absys-depth-first` | `--search depth-first` | `mixed`: every derivation is held at once, but only the first running one is elaborated until it hibernates or fails (systems file, Units) |
| `absys-wake-back` | `--wake back` | `all-live` |

Every run also passes `--notation N` (from the program's file name, below)
and `--steps B`, the problem's budget. All three modes are allowed for
every configuration. Every configuration is incremental
(`run.posing: "incremental"`).

**The binary.** Every mode runs `absys-measure` (branch `measure`: the
pinned `efd5203` with `--measure` and `--full` added; `5450449` in
`cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0`, `8a0eefd` in `cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0-m2`,
which adds `--peak-every`, section 4). Its commit is read from
`/opt/src/COMMITS`. Behaviour runs pass `--full` and not `--measure`: `--full` only
prints lists and derivations without cutting them short, so that
`observe()` and `answers()` read every answer (systems file, Output). The
qualification shows its output identical to the baseline `absys`'s on
every test (QUESTIONS, A2). `system_build.commit` is `5450449…`, read from
`/opt/src/COMMITS`, and `instrumented: true`.

Two more environment variables: `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1` makes storage
runs take the peak after every step (section 4), for small-scale
validation; `HARNESS_RUN_LABEL`, if set, is copied verbatim into the
record's `notes`. Absys has no version option,
so `version_output` is `null`.

## 3. The program contract

A program author cannot run the program before its results are taken, so
everything below is exact. Only `check` may be used before the program is
fixed.

### 3.1 The file

One file, UTF-8. **Its extension fixes the notation**, as the system's own
rule does (`src/session.rs`, `notation_for`): `.ab1` is the 1969 notation
(Absys 1, with arithmetic), `.ab2` the 1982 notation, anything else (use
`.abs`) the 1990 notation. Lines beginning with `%` are comments in all
three; the harness's markers are comments, so they are not tokens.

The file is divided by marker lines (each on its own line; leading spaces
allowed; exact patterns):

| marker | pattern | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `% STAGE k` | `^\s*%\s*STAGE\s+(\d+)\s*$` | the text of stage *k* starts here |
| `% PART name` | `^\s*%\s*PART\s+(\S+)\s*$` | the text of the part *name* starts here (3.5); a program has STAGE sections or PART sections, not both |
| `% SPAWN c` | `^\s*%\s*SPAWN\s+(\S+)\s*$` | inside a stage's section: the text of the spawned computation *c* starts here (3.6) |
| `% PARAMETERS n order …` | `^\s*%\s*PARAMETERS\b(.*)$` | in the prelude: the instance parameters the program wants (3.4) |
| `% CONSTANTS BEGIN` / `% CONSTANTS END` | a comment line containing the words | the constants block (3.9), in the prelude: a table the harness reads, never given to the system |

Everything before the first STAGE or PART marker is the **prelude**: the
definitions of the problem's relations and the constants block. A section
runs to the next STAGE or PART marker (a SPAWN subsection to the next
SPAWN, STAGE or PART marker). Marker lines are given to the system with
the section they begin; they are comments.

### 3.2 How a stage is given to the system

**Behaviour runs** start one `absys-measure repl` process and keep it for
the whole run: every stage is received into the same session, as the
systems file says ("The same computation"). The harness writes to its
standard input, in this order:

1. at stage 1: one assertion per declared parameter (3.4), then the
   prelude's lines (without the constants block), then stage 1's section;
2. at stage *k*: stage *k*'s section, as the file has it but with each
   constant's name replaced by its value (3.9), line by line, **only when
   stage *k* is posed**. No line of a later section is
   ever written before its stage (no anticipation), and the program is
   never told how many stages follow.

After each section, and after each piece of 1 (the parameters, the
prelude), the harness writes a line `.help`. The repl's reply to it is a
fixed text, which tells the harness that the system has finished with
everything before it (QUESTIONS, A3). The repl takes each line in turn and
does everything that can be done before it reads the next (each
assertion is elaborated until every derivation hibernates or fails, or the
budget runs out).

**The repl reads a text line by line**, and that is the one constraint it
puts on layout (`src/main.rs`, `repl`). After each line it parses what it
has read since the last complete assertion:

- if that parses, it is accepted at once, as one or more assertions;
- if it fails to parse only because it ends too soon, the repl reads on;
- otherwise it reports `error at L:C: message` and drops it.

So, **a program must keep these rules**, which `check` enforces:

1. **An assertion that spans several lines must not be complete at the
   end of any of its lines but the last.** End a line with `or`, `,`,
   an open `{` or `[`, or `=`, never at a point where the assertion could
   end. `colour = lambda C {C = 'red'} or` followed by `{C = 'green'}` is
   right; `colour = lambda C {C = 'red'}` followed by a line
   `or {C = 'green'}` is two assertions to the repl, the second a syntax
   error.
2. **Every section ends with a complete assertion.** Otherwise the repl
   reads the harness's `.help` as the assertion's continuation and
   reports a syntax error (``error at L:1: `.` is not in the notation``),
   which the harness records as the stage's error.
3. **No line, outside an unfinished assertion, may begin with `?` or
   `.`.** The repl takes such a line as a command (`.quit` ends it).

**Cost and storage runs** cannot use the repl, which reports no step
count and no store: the system reports them only for a whole text,
`absys-measure FILE --measure`. So each stage *k* is one new process on a
text the harness writes: the parameters' assertions, the prelude and the
sections of stages 1 to *k*, in order, exactly as above. Its session takes
the assertions one at a time, as the repl's does, and the qualification
shows that its states and step counts at every stage are those of the
incremental behaviour run. These records show every stage after the first
as `reposed` (`reason: "configuration"`), with the steps of stages 1 to
*k*−1 as restart cost, which the behaviour run does not pay (QUESTIONS,
A4).

### 3.3 What the program writes in a stage's section

The stage's information, as Absys assertions: equations, applications,
`or`, `not`, `set`, `tout`, procedure definitions (a stage may define a
procedure, P08 for instance). A replacing or retracting stage (P10, P15d)
is whatever assertions the program uses to carry it out; the harness
gives the section as written, every one of them, on every replay.

**Identifiers.** As the reconstruction decides (`docs/decisions.md`, rule
6): outside any lambda every identifier is shared by the whole text, so a
name given a value in the prelude, the constants block or an earlier
stage is the same variable in every later stage. In the 1990 notation,
inside a lambda an identifier with a capital that the lambda does not
bind is local, and one with a small letter is shared; in the 1969
notation a primed name is local; in the 1982 notation, a name the body
uses but never applies, and the lambda does not bind, is local. So a
constant used inside a lambda must be written with a small letter (1990)
or not be primed (1969).

**Name each unknown as `stages.json` names it** (`x`, `total`, …), where
the notation allows it: `observe()` asks the system for each unknown by
that name (3.8). Every identifier of the text that is not a procedure is
printed in every derivation, so the parameters' names appear in the
answers too. The constants' names do not: the system never sees them
(3.9).

### 3.4 Instance parameters

A program that needs an instance's parameters (n, an order, a spawn
order, the answer mode) names them on one line of the prelude:

    % PARAMETERS n order

For each name, in that order, the harness gives the system, at stage 1,
before the prelude, one assertion `NAME = VALUE`, in the program's
notation:

| value | 1990 (`.abs`) | 1969 (`.ab1`) | 1982 (`.ab2`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"n": 1000` | `n = 1000` | `n = 1000` | `n = 1000` |
| `"order": ["R2", "R1", "R3"]` | `order = ['R2', 'R1', 'R3']` | `order = ['R2';'R1';'R3']` | `order = ['R2','R1','R3']` |
| `"answers": "all"` | `answers = 'all'` | `answers = 'all'` | `answers = 'all'` |
| `"spawn_order": ["A", "B"]` | `spawn_order = ['A', 'B']` | `spawn_order = ['A';'B']` | `spawn_order = ['A','B']` |

The names are `n`, `order`, `answers`, `cap` and `spawn_order`, and only
those the instance has (`stages.json`). A program that declares none gets
none. The record lists what was passed (`posed.instance_parameters_passed`).
The harness never passes a constant of a problem.

The answer mode needs nothing from the program: the harness's cap does it
(3.7). The spawn order needs nothing either (3.6).

### 3.5 Arrival orders of written relations: PART sections (P02b, P07a)

Where an instance's `order` names the stage's relations (`P02b.R2R1R3`:
R2, then R1, then R3; `P07a.312`: the third relation written, then the
first, then the second), a program may give each relation as a part,
named as the order names it:

    % PART R1
    ...
    % PART R2
    ...

At stage *k* the harness gives part `order[k-1]`. A program for the
instance in the written order (`P07a`, order `["1","2","3"]`) is the same
program. Orders that do not name stages (P16's `ascending`, …) are passed
only as the parameter `order` (3.4), and the program must use it itself.

### 3.6 Spawned computations (P09a, P09b, P16b)

A stage that spawns computations has, in its section, one SPAWN
subsection per computation, named as `stages.json` names them:

    % STAGE 1
    % SPAWN A
    ...
    % SPAWN B
    ...

Text in the section before the first SPAWN is given first. Then, for each
computation in the instance's `spawn_order` (or the order of the stage's
`spawns`), the harness gives its subsection, waits until the system has
done everything it can (every derivation hibernates or fails, or the
budget runs out), reads that computation's answers and state, and then
gives the next (`side_by_side: false`).

**Absys has no separate computations**: one session holds one
computation, whose derivations every assertion is added to. A spawned
computation's text is accepted into that one computation, conjoined with
everything already there, and so it shares every unknown with the others
(QUESTIONS, A5). P16b's contributors are therefore spawned, not posed by
the fallback. Whether P09a ("not conjoined") is expressible in Absys is
for the program author and the classifiers; the harness does nothing to
separate them.

### 3.7 Answers: the system's standard mechanism

Absys reports a computation as its **derivations**, every one at once,
each with its bindings, the processes it suspends and its outputs, by
printing its state. That is the standard mechanism, and the program needs
nothing to use it. `answers(cap)` is the first `cap` derivations of the
state the system prints at the end of the stage (the repl's `?`), each
derivation's block verbatim, from its line `  derivation #N (…)` to the
next. Under `--full` every derivation is printed.

| ended_by | when |
|---|---|
| `exhausted` | the system printed at most `cap` derivations (none, when no derivation survives) |
| `cap` | it printed more than `cap`; the rest are in `observe.raw` |
| `budget` | its state reports derivations still elaborating when the budget ran out |
| `error` | the system reported an error for the stage's text |
| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |

Absys elaborates every derivation before it reports any, so there is no
request for "more answers": a stage never ends *alternatives pending*
(QUESTIONS, A8). In cost mode each answer's `steps_at` is the stage's
steps, when the mechanism gave every answer at once.

### 3.8 What `observe()` and `print()` read

At the end of each stage (and for each spawned computation, after its
section) the harness writes the repl's own commands:

- `?`: the state, every derivation with its status (`hibernating` or
  `still elaborating`), its outputs, its procedures, every identifier's
  value (with `(suspended: …)` where only suspended equations constrain
  it), its suspended processes, and what is still to do. This is
  `print`, and the start of `observe.raw`;
- `? NAME`, for each unknown of the sub-problem in `stages.json` written
  as a plain identifier: the system's value of NAME in each derivation
  (`#3: x = 2`), or `NAME does not occur`. These are `observe.bindings`,
  by unknown, verbatim, and follow in `observe.raw`.

Both read and change nothing. In cost and storage runs, `print` and
`observe.raw` are the state `absys FILE` prints at the end of the text of
stages 1 to *k* (with `--each` in a stage that spawns, the state after
each assertion, from which each computation's is read).

### 3.9 The constants block

Every constant of every stage is in **one block in the prelude**, between
a comment line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and one containing
`CONSTANTS END`. The block is a **table, never given to the system**: one
constant per line, `NAME = VALUE`, the value on that line (comment lines
and blank lines are allowed; a `%` ends the value):

    % CONSTANTS BEGIN
    c1 = 41
    c2 = 'red'
    facts = [[1, 'a'], [2, 'b']]
    % CONSTANTS END

The program's text refers to the constants by name (`pr = [c1, d]`).
**When the harness gives a section to the system, it replaces each name
of the table, in that section's text, by its value**, so that what the
system receives is `pr = [41, d]`. A constant therefore reaches the system
only with the section that uses it: a constant of stage 3 is not in the
system, as information or as a name, before stage 3 is posed (no
anticipation, `PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5). A name used in
the prelude (in a definition) is given with the prelude, at stage 1.

What is replaced, exactly: an identifier (the system's: a letter or `_`,
then letters, digits and `_`, and, after a small letter, `-` between
letters, as in `math-course`) equal to a name of the table. Nothing is
replaced inside a quoted constant (`'…'`, `"…"`), inside a comment, or in
a name written with a prime (1969: a new local name). The value is put in
as written in the table, with no change. So:

- name constants with identifiers that the program uses for nothing else;
- a constant used inside a lambda is replaced like any other (the value,
  not the name, reaches the system, so the scoping rules of 3.3 do not
  arise).

The verifier replaces only the lines between the markers. The harness
records `constants.how: "block"` when the markers are present, else
`"none"`. `check` parses each section after the replacement, as the
system will receive it, and reports a line of the block that is not
`NAME = VALUE`. Absys reads no input, so there is no `input` form.

### 3.10 Effects (P11): emit

The harness's `emit(m)` is written, in Absys,

    tout("emit", M)

with the term to emit as its second argument. `tout` is the system's own
output assertion (Elcock 1990, note 11): it waits until its term has no
uninstantiated variable, and then performs one output, `emit = VALUE`, in
the derivation it is in. In P11 runs the harness switches the system's
trace on (`.trace`, or `--trace`), and every `output` event of the trace
whose text begins `emit = ` becomes one entry of the log, `entry` being
the rest of it, the system's rendering of the term (`'red'`, `[1,2]`), in
the order the trace shows them. An output performed in a derivation that
later fails stays in the log: nothing the system does removes an entry.
Entries made while a reposed run replays an earlier stage carry
`during_replay_of`. Behaviour runs write to
`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects.jsonl`; the separate run that measures a
restart cost, and every cost and storage run, write to
`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl`. Neither is ever reset.

**Commit stages** (P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2): Absys keeps every
derivation live and selects none. The section may be empty (comments
only). `answers(1)` reports the first derivation printed, as for any
any-one query; no commitment is recorded, and none is replayed when a
later stage is reposed (QUESTIONS, A6).

### 3.11 Provenance

At the top of the file, in comments, the lines `% AUTHOR: …`,
`% PRECURSOR-SEEN: yes|no` (whether its author had seen the E01–E09
programs) and `% IDIOM: …` (the source of each idiom). `check` warns if
there is no `AUTHOR` line.

### 3.12 H tokens

`METRICS.md`, class H: the harness's own calls as they appear in a
program. In an Absys program they are:

| construct | H tokens |
|---|---|
| the emit stub's binding, `tout("emit", T)` | `tout`, `(`, `"emit"`, `,` and `)`; the term `T` is classed on its own (rule 10) |

Nothing else in a program is H. The markers are comments; the parameter
assertions are written by the harness, not the program; answers are
collected from what the system prints by itself, with no call in the
program, so there is no output adapter. A program's uses of a parameter's
name (`n`), its constants block and its definitions are classed by the
rules of `METRICS.md`.

### 3.13 A complete minimal example

A made-up problem, not one of P01–P16 (`qualification/stages-qualification.json`, X10):

> **X10a.** `pair(A, B, P)` holds when P is the list `[A, B]`.
> Stage 1: `pair(a, b, pr)`. Stage 2: `pr = [⟨k⟩, d]`. Stage 3: `d = ⟨atom⟩`.
> Unknowns a, b, pr, d. Constants: ⟨k⟩ = 41, ⟨atom⟩ = `'red'`.

The program, `qualification/programs/x10-pair.abs`:

```
% AUTHOR: harness-absys (an agent), for the harness's qualification. MADE UP: not a problem program.
% PRECURSOR-SEEN: no. IDIOM: a lambda procedure, as in Elcock 1990 p. 8.
% CONSTANTS BEGIN
c1 = 41
c2 = 'red'
% CONSTANTS END
pair = lambda A, B, P {P = [A, B]}
% STAGE 1
pair(a, b, pr)
% STAGE 2
pr = [c1, d]
% STAGE 3
d = c2
```

What the system receives, in one session, and what the harness collects
(from the qualification's behaviour record):

| stage | written to the repl | `answers(20)`: the one derivation | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the prelude without the block (lines 1, 2 and 7), `.help`, `% STAGE 1` and `pair(a, b, pr)`, `.help`, then `?` and `? a`, `? b`, `? pr`, `? d` | `a  uninstantiated`, `b  uninstantiated`, `pr = [a,b]` | finished |
| 2 | `% STAGE 2`, `pr = [41, d]`, `.help`, `?`, … | `a = 41`, `b = d   (suspended: b = d)`, `pr = [41,b]`, `suspended   b = d` | suspended |
| 3 | `% STAGE 3`, `d = 'red'`, `.help`, `?`, … | `a = 41`, `b = 'red'`, `pr = [41,'red']`, `d = 'red'` | finished |

41 is not in the system before stage 2, nor `'red'` before stage 3.

Its H tokens: none. Snippets for the other forms are in
`qualification/programs/`: SPAWN (`x17-spawn.abs`), PART with a parameter
(`x19-parts.abs`), emit (`x18-emit.abs`), the 1969 notation
(`x20-arith.ab1`).

## 4. Modes

| mode | process | what is of record |
|---|---|---|
| behaviour | one `absys-measure repl --full` for the run (a new one only to repose) | answers, `observe`, `print`, execution state, the effects log. No step count: the repl reports none |
| cost | per stage, `absys-measure FILE --measure --peak-every 0 --full` on stages 1..k; `--trace` too where the budget is 10⁶ | `steps.stage` (the steps of stage k's assertions: the incremental cost), `steps.restated` (all of the run), `restart_cost` (stages 1..k−1, in-run), `to_end`, `repeated_work` |
| storage | the same command with `--peak-every 1000` (`1` under `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1`), and `--trace` only in P11 | the store vector, `alternatives.peak` (derivations, exact), the state's suspended processes |

- **Steps** are the system's (one step of the machine, as `--steps`
  counts them), read only from `--measure`'s table, the systems file's
  qualified measurement. Sampling the store adds time, not steps
  (systems file). Cost and storage records both keep what `--measure`
  gave; the figure of record is the mode's. Behaviour records have
  `steps.stage: null`.
- **Store** (`store.quantities`): the ten quantities of `--measure`, each
  with `boundary`, after the stage's last assertion (exact in every
  setting), and `peak`, which depends on how often the system takes it
  (`--peak-every`, absys-measure `8a0eefd`; QUESTIONS, A15):

  | run | `--peak-every` | `peak` |
  |---|---|---|
  | cost | 0: only when an assertion is added and when its elaboration ends | `null`, with a note: not a peak |
  | storage | 1000: every 1000 steps, and at the start and end of each assertion | `kind: "sampled"`, `sample_interval`: "every 1000 steps, and at the start and end of each assertion (absys-measure --peak-every 1000)" |
  | storage, `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1` | 1: after every step | `kind: "exact"` |
  | either, with a build that rejects `--peak-every` (`5450449`) | not passed: after every step | `kind: "exact"`, as before |

  `alternatives.peak` (derivations) follows the same rule. Step counts and
  standard output are the same at every setting. A stage with no
  assertion has the boundary of the last assertion before it and no peak.
- **Suspended work** (`suspended`) is what the system prints as suspended,
  in every mode, counted by kind under `--measure`'s names
  (`susp_equations` for an equation between unknowns, `susp_applications`
  for "waits for a definition" or "for its key", `susp_relations` for
  "waits for two of its numbers" or "for its term", `susp_negations` for
  "waits for its variables" or "cannot be decided yet"), summed over
  derivations. The printer shows only processes still waiting on an
  uninstantiated variable; `--measure`'s `susp_*` in the store also count
  equations and arithmetic relations that stay associated with their
  variables after every one is bound (`docs/decisions.md`, rule 10), so
  the two may differ.
- **Repeated work** (cost mode, budget 10⁶): `reactivating_events`, the
  number of trace events of the stage's assertions that reactivated
  suspended processes (`… reactivated …`: a variable was bound and the
  processes waiting on it went back to the goal). Not measured (`null`)
  where the budget is 10⁸, whose traces would be too large to keep.
- **P13**: `cpu_time_s` and `max_rss_kb` of the behaviour run's process
  (`getrusage` through `os.wait4`), for growth only.

## 5. Budget, safety limit, reposing

- **Budget.** `--steps B`, B the problem's budget, is the system's own
  budget, and it counts **per assertion**: each assertion is elaborated
  for at most B steps. A stage of several assertions can therefore spend
  more than B in all before the system reports budget (QUESTIONS, A1);
  cost records say so in a note when it happens. A stage is *budget* when
  the system's state reports derivations "still elaborating when the
  budget ran out".
- **Continuing after budget: yes, in every configuration.** The derivations
  still elaborating stay in the session, and the next assertion accepted
  goes on elaborating them, with a new budget. So after *budget* the next
  stage is posed into the same session, `continued_after_budget: true`.
- **Safety limit.** For an incremental stage, from writing its first line
  to reading the last reply; for a reposed one, the whole run, replay
  included. When it is reached the harness sends **SIGKILL** to the
  system's process (`safety_limit.how_stopped`), records what it had read,
  and, where the problem allows, reruns the stage once with the raised
  limit, by reposing (the session is gone). P12, P13 and P16: no rerun.
- **Reposing** (after *error*, after a final *timeout*, a safety rerun):
  a new session, into which the harness writes the parameters, the
  prelude and every section of stages 1 to *k*−1 in order, each followed
  by `.help`, replacements and withdrawals included, then stage *k* as
  usual. The repl gives no step count, so the restart cost is measured on
  a **separate run** of that same text with `absys-measure json`, which
  reports each assertion's steps (the same count as `--measure`'s, as the
  qualification shows) without sampling the store
  (`restart_cost_method: "separate-run"`). It stops at a syntax error,
  where the repl goes on, so after an error it may undercount, and the
  record says so in `harness_faults`.
- **Error.** The repl reports a syntax or static error and goes on; the
  harness records the stage as *error* with the message verbatim, and
  poses the next stage by reposing, as `PROTOCOL.md` says. A system
  process that ends on its own (a crash, or killed by the kernel) is
  *error* too, with its exit status or signal.
- **When a reposed stage's replay itself cannot finish** (the replay is
  killed for lack of memory), no restart cost can be measured, and the
  record does not validate: it is kept as `.INVALID.json`, exit 3
  (QUESTIONS, A12).

## 6. `check`

    harnesses/absys/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM

Absys has no parse-only mode. `absys lsp` cannot serve: its diagnostics
*run* the text (`src/lsp.rs`, `analyse`, with a budget of 20 000 steps).
So `check` does this, the same for every configuration (the flags change
nothing a parser sees):

1. It reads the program's bytes and finds its sections, as `run` does
   (3.1); it reports misplaced markers, numbering, and a missing `AUTHOR`
   line (a warning).
2. For each section, as the harness would give it, it does what the repl
   does line by line (3.2): after each line, it gives the text read since
   the last complete assertion to `absys-measure json FILE --steps 0`.
   That command parses the text and compiles each assertion and adds it
   to the goal, with **a budget of zero steps**: no step of the machine
   is taken, so no equation, application, `or`, `not`, `set` or `tout` is
   elaborated. `check` reads only the error (with its line and column)
   and the number of assertions, and stops if the system reports any step
   or event at all.
3. It prints each error verbatim, with its line in the program, each line
   that the repl would take as a command, and each section that ends in
   an unfinished assertion. Exit 0 when there is none, 1 otherwise.

It never prints anything the program would compute. The qualification
shows it on a program whose only effect, run, is to output a marker: the
marker is not in `check`'s output, while running the program prints it.
Absys has no means of writing a file, so no file test is possible.

## 7. Confounds

Everything the harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers
through the system's mechanism and reading state (copied into every
record's `run.confounds`):

1. Behaviour runs use the measurement build with `--full` (printer only),
   not the baseline build (2).
2. The `.help` line after each section, to know where the system's output
   for it ends; a section ending inside an unfinished assertion turns it
   into a syntax error (3.2).
3. `?` and `? NAME` to read the state (3.8).
4. The parameters' assertions, written by the harness (3.4).
5. PART sections chosen by the instance's order (3.5).
6. Spawned computations accepted one after another into the one session,
   each read right after its section (3.6).
7. The budget is per assertion (5).
8. Cost and storage runs are a new process per stage, on stages 1..k (3.2).
9. The restart cost of a reposed behaviour stage is measured on a separate
   `json` run (5).
10. The trace is switched on in P11 runs and in cost runs with the 10⁶
    budget (3.10, 4).
11. `answers(cap)` takes the first `cap` derivations of the printed state (3.7).
12. Each constant's name is replaced by its value in the section that uses
    it, when that section is given; the block itself is never given (3.9).

## 8. Qualification

`qualification/run-qualification` reruns everything; its output is
`qualification/output.txt`, and its records are in
`qualification/records/`. See [`qualification/README.md`](qualification/README.md).

# Protocol

*Draft 0.7.*

## Phases

1. **Draft.** `SPECIFICATION.md`, `METRICS.md`, this file and `problems/`
   are written. No program for the study is written, apart from the
   calibration programs (`METRICS.md`, Calibration), which are development
   examples and never results.
   Measurement may be qualified at this phase: establishing what each
   system can report, and adding instrumentation that changes no result,
   under the conditions in "Instrumentation" below.
2. **Independent review.** A reviewer who has not written the draft reads
   it for ambiguity, for errors in the valid outcomes, for language bias,
   and for problems missing from the suite. Findings and responses are kept
   in `reviews/`. *(Draft 0.1 had one review, answered in draft 0.2. Draft
   0.3 had a second, by a fresh reviewer, answered in draft 0.4. Draft 0.5
   had a third, answered in draft 0.6. Draft 0.7 is the freeze candidate.)*
3. **Freeze.** The specification is tagged `spec-1.0`, together with:
   - the pinned version or commit of every system in the first comparison;
   - each systems file's cores, flags and units;
   - the generic harness interface below.

   From then on, these change only by amendment.
4. **Harnesses.** One harness per system implements the interface, and is
   published before any program is run.
5. **Implementation.** Programs are written for each configuration from the
   problem files, one per configuration and problem, fixed before any of
   them is run.
6. **Results.** Each program is run and classified, and the results are
   recorded in `results/`.
7. **Comparison.** Only after results exist for at least two systems on
   every problem.

No system is implemented before the freeze. The benchmark is not changed
afterwards to suit any system, including PLANNER and the systems after it.

## Amendments

An amendment is a numbered, dated change to a frozen file, with its reason.
It applies to every system. Results obtained before it are kept, marked
with the specification version they were obtained under, and rerun under
the new version.

A problem proposed after the freeze does not join the frozen suite. It goes
into a separate, dated supplementary suite, reported apart from the frozen
one, with the date it was proposed and the results that existed then.

## Roles

| role | does | has access to |
|---|---|---|
| **specification author** | writes the problems and the protocol | the public repository |
| **variant custodian** | writes the hidden variants and their valid outcomes | the specification, and the private variants |
| **implementation author** | writes the programs | the public repository only |
| **harness author** | writes each system's harness (phase 4) | the public repository |
| **classifier A** | classes the programs' constructs, and the outcomes of every run on all axes, checking residual equivalence | the specification, the metrics, the programs, their outputs and the valid outcomes |
| **classifier B** | does both independently | the same, without A's classes |
| **verifier** | runs the programs on the hidden variants | the programs, the variants and their outcomes |

Each role is a separate agent or person, with its own context, and its
provenance is recorded. The two classifiers are of different origin (for
instance Claude and Codex), and neither wrote the program it classes.
Their disagreements, on tokens and on outcomes, are recorded, and a
disputed outcome is reported under both classes.

**Hidden variants** are made inaccessible, not merely placed where an
implementation author is told not to look. *(For wave 1, amended:
`AMENDMENTS.md`, 1.)* The custodian writes them
before the freeze and encrypts them with a key the project's owner holds
but does not use. The plaintext begins with a random nonce of at least 128
bits, so that a small space of constants cannot be recovered from its
hash. Only the ciphertext and the SHA-256 hash of the plaintext are
committed. The key is given to the verifier only after every primary
program and its results are committed. The verifier publishes the
plaintext, and anyone can check it against the hash. Each later wave of
systems (PLANNER onwards) has its own sealed set, made before that wave's
programs are written, since revealing a set publishes it.

## Evidence classification

Every implementation is given one or more of these classes:

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| **original** | a surviving historical implementation, on the hardware or software it was written for |
| **rehosted** | a surviving historical implementation, running in a modern environment (an emulator, a port of the original source) |
| **reconstructed** | a modern implementation derived from historical documents, where no implementation survives |
| **modern** | a contemporary implementation of the language |
| **extended** | mechanisms supplied for the experiment, beyond the implementation's own |

Two qualifiers may be attached to a class:

- *with external mechanisms*: libraries or run-time features outside the
  configuration's core are used (`METRICS.md`);
- *alternative reading*: a reconstruction run with a decision taken the
  other way, where its sources conflict.

Results are always reported with the class. No result from a modern or
extended configuration is attributed to the historical language. Where a
language was described more fully than it was implemented (PLANNER and
Micro-Planner, for instance), the described language and the implemented
subset are separate systems.

## Configurations

A configuration is one system with a stated set of mechanisms. Results are
kept separate per configuration, so that a capability introduced later is
not attributed to the earlier model. Each systems file lists, per
configuration:

- its core, built-in by built-in;
- its flags;
- the unit of steps, of an alternative and of store, and how each is
  measured;
- what "the same computation" means. That is, whether a stage can be
  received into a computation already running, and how.

A reconstruction is pinned at a commit when the specification is frozen.
Any later change to it, for whatever reason, makes a new configuration,
reported separately, and never replaces the pinned one.

## Instrumentation

A measurement added to a system must not change what it computes. For a
reconstruction:

- the unmodified commit is kept as the baseline;
- instrumentation is made on a separate branch, and recorded as its own
  commit;
- it may not change scheduling, search, equality, suspension or any other
  rule of the machine;
- the instrumented build, with measurement on and off, must give output
  identical to the baseline's, byte for byte, on every example and in every
  output mode, including full traces. The check and its result are
  recorded.

## The harness interface

Every harness provides exactly these operations, and nothing that orders,
chooses or re-poses goals on its own:

- **pose(stage)**: give the system the information of one stage, into the
  same computation if the configuration allows it, or else by reposing.
  A reposed run replays **every** stage 1 to k in order, replacements and
  withdrawals included, and the program must carry them out. The harness
  never works out the net information itself;
- **spawn(computation)**: start a separate computation in the same
  instance (P09), returning at once where the configuration can run
  computations side by side. In a configuration that cannot, the first
  runs to its end or its budget, and then the next;
- **answers(cap)**: collect the answers the system reports, through its
  standard mechanism for enumerating them, until it is exhausted, the
  budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected. `cap` is 1 for an
  *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as each problem states. The execution
  state is classified after the call;
- **observe()**: record the state the common observations need, including
  bindings the system holds (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported");
- **print()**.

Each system's systems file says what its standard mechanism for answers
is. For Python and ALGOL 60, it is the values the program prints.

**Observing must not consume the computation.** In a system where
collecting answers would end or alter the computation that the next stage
extends (exhausting a backtracking search, for instance), the observation
of stage k is taken on a separate run of stages 1 to k. The incremental
run is left as it was.

**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** When a commit stage
has selected an outcome v (P11), a reposed run replays it as the
information x = v. It does not ask the system to select again, which could
commit to a different outcome.

**External effects** (P11) are written to one log per problem, never reset,
across every run the harness makes for classification, reposed runs
included. Separate observation runs write to a separate log, which is not
judged. Entries that are duplicated only because a run was reposed are
counted separately, as the cost of reposing an irreversible effect.

Concurrency used to run computations (threads, processes) is a mechanism of
the configuration, listed in its systems file. A harness may not run
computations concurrently itself. In P09, all computations run in one
instance of the system, sharing one database, never in separate operating
system processes.

## Writing a program

1. Write it from the problem file. Programs written for this study's
   precursors (the absys experiments E01–E09) exist, and their author may
   have seen them; each program says whether its author had.
2. Use the idioms of the system's period where they are known. Cite the
   source of each idiom: a manual, a paper or a published program.
3. Transcribe the definitions given. Anything else is reformulation, and
   counts as R.
4. Where several idiomatic programs are possible, choose one per
   configuration and problem before any is run, or run and report every
   variant. In either case, one is designated the **primary** variant
   before any is run, and stands for the configuration.
5. **No anticipation.** The code that handles stage k may not depend on the
   content of any later stage.
6. **Genericity.** A program must stay correct when the constants in a
   problem's stages are changed. It keeps them in one marked place, or reads
   them as input, so that the verifier can substitute them. Each problem
   has hidden variants with other constants, held by someone who does not
   write programs. Every program is run on them after its results are
   recorded. The custodian works out each variant's valid outcomes
   independently, stage by stage, as the problem files give them for the
   original constants. A variant's outcomes need not have the same classes
   as the original's: other constants can make a finite outcome infinite,
   or a consistent stage inconsistent. A program's run on a variant is
   classified against **that variant's** valid outcomes, on the semantic and
   effects axes, exactly as a primary run is. A program **fails** a variant
   where that classification differs from its classification on the
   original constants, each against its own valid outcomes: a program
   complete on the original and unsound on the variant fails it. It is
   recorded as such, since it encodes a conclusion rather than computing
   it. The custodian records, for each variant, which of the original's
   outcome classes it was built to keep, if any.
7. A program may not be revised after its results are seen, except to fix a
   transcription error: a place where the program departs from the text of
   the problem file. Each fix is recorded as a diff, with the reason. A
   program changed for any other reason is a separate, named variant, and
   is reported as such.
8. Record the author of each program, human or agent.

## Running

- Pin the version of every system, and record its source and commit.
- **Budget.** 10⁶ steps in the system's own unit, per stage and per
  computation. In P09, each separate computation has its own budget and its
  own classification. A reposed run of stages 1 to k has a budget of its
  measured restart cost plus 10⁶.
- **The budget is relative to each system.** 10⁶ Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
  inferences and Python instructions are different amounts of work. So
  *budget* is a classification within a system, and is not compared
  across systems. Each system records, as a calibration figure, its steps
  for P13b at n = 10³, or, where P13b is not expressible, for P03e.
- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
  computation, with a new budget. Whether it can is recorded, since
  continuing past an exhausted budget is itself a capability. Stages 1 to
  k+1 are reposed only when the configuration cannot continue, and the
  reposing counts under restart cost.
- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1, counted
  under restart cost.
- **Safety limit.** A limit of 60 seconds per stage protects the harness.
  It is not a measurement. A stage it stops is rerun once, with the limit
  raised tenfold. If the rerun also stops, *timeout* is final for that
  stage. Both runs are recorded. Answers reported before the limit stopped
  the run are kept and classified on the semantic axis; only the execution
  state is *timeout*.

## Modes of running

Each program is run in up to three modes:

| mode | what it establishes | instrumentation |
|---|---|---|
| **behaviour** | the outcomes, the three axes and effects | none beyond the harness |
| **cost** | steps, answer latency, problem-defined operation counts | step counting only |
| **storage** | store, retained alternatives, suspended state | the systems file's storage measurement |

- The semantic result and execution state are taken from the behaviour run.
- Where two modes can be compared, their semantic results must agree, and
  any disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation.
- A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
  count or the classification, because sampling adds steps of its own.
- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (in
  cost or storage mode, when the behaviour run finished) is not evidence
  that the model cannot complete the problem. It is recorded as a limit of
  the measurement.
- Run in CI where the system allows it, and compare with recorded output.

## Recording a result

Each result is a file `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>.md` that
gives:

- the specification version, the system version or commit, the
  configuration and the evidence class;
- the program, or a link to it at a commit, and whether its author had seen
  a precursor;
- for each stage, the common observations of `SPECIFICATION.md` and the
  problem's own;
- the token counts by class, per classifier, with the disputed tokens;
- the configuration's expressibility for the problem;
- the supporting code (S) used, by mechanism. An *extended* result is named
  by its mechanism. Every configuration's S mechanisms are listed, with
  their size, at phase 4, before any program is run;
- whether the program passed its hidden variants.

## Guarding against bias

- The reasons for choosing a problem, and the history of each system's
  implementation, are disclosed.
- Every review is asked for problems that favour designs other than those
  the suite came from.
- Results are reported for every system on every problem, including
  "not expressible".
- Both classifiers' token classes are kept and reported for every result,
  throughout the study, never only an adjudicated set. A comparative
  conclusion that would change if one classifier's classes were used in
  place of the other's is reported as **classification-sensitive**, with
  both figures.
- No ranking is computed. A summary may say where a system needed control,
  supporting code or intervention that another did not, and what it held in
  store to avoid them.
- Interpretation, including any connection to later work, is kept out of
  `results/` and in a separate document written after the comparison.

# Independent classification: absys, batch 1B, P05

Classifier: Codex, independent classifier B. The source repository is the clone named in the brief, "'`~/cp-roles/classifier-1B-B3`, at the user-stated commit `1f291be`. I did not write the programs, inspect another classifier'"'s work, run a program, run the system, or modify the source clone. All generated files are in the authorized output directory.

## Scope and evidence

The text manifest contains P05a.ab1, P05b.ab1 and P05c.ab1 under "'`absys/`; each is shared byte for byte by `absys-depth-first` and `absys-wake-back`. Token classes do not depend on configuration, so the JSON classes only those first paths. Frozen token TSV indices are used directly; no re-tokenization was performed. No P08 or named P05 program variant occurs in the permitted records inspected. `late_definition` is therefore empty.

I inspected all 27 P05 raw records (nine behaviour, nine cost, nine storage), including INVALID records, and all six labelled m2 measurement reruns. Large gzip records were decoded and summarized by the local `summarize_records.py`; they were not dumped wholesale. `build_classification.py` builds the JSON and checks token coverage, behaviour-stage coverage, fault flags, and agreement of the m2 classifications. The supporting `record_summaries.json` contains extracted evidence, not another classifier'"'s judgements.

The principal normative files consulted were README.md, SPECIFICATION.md, METRICS.md, PROTOCOL.md, AMENDMENTS.md, problems/README.md and problems/05-late-contradiction.md. Contract evidence came from systems/absys/README.md, harnesses/README.md, harnesses/stages.json, harnesses/record.schema.json, harnesses/absys/README.md, harnesses/absys/S-mechanisms.md and relevant sections of harnesses/absys/absys_harness.py. The three P05 programs in each configuration, their frozen token files, the text manifest, permitted P05 records, and the two permitted batch logs supplied the remaining evidence.

**Files read outside the allowed list: none.** References to prohibited files within allowed documents and program comments were not followed. No web access was used.

## Token decisions

"'`pick` transcribes the stated three closed-world facts in the specified order. Its definition and its applications are P (class P, rules 1 and 6). The constants-table assignments are P: their contents are the problem'"'s stage information, even though the harness substitutes them and does not send the table itself. Absys harness section 3.12 explicitly says that such a table is not automatically H.

In P05a, gt tokens 19–35, pos 36–56, ne 57–79, and their stage applications 99–104 and 105–110 are R. In P05b, gt 19–35, pos 36–56 and the stage application 69–74 are R. The introduced arithmetic differences, positive-integer cases, intermediate names, and alternative definition of integer disequality are not definitions given by P05. They implement semantic reformulations, rather than a general constraint mechanism. These are R constructs throughout; arithmetic on an invented intermediate is not an unchanged P05 conjunct merely because addition is primitive. Rule 10 is applied by the roles of the nested constructs.

The closest token ambiguity is pos versus C under rule 6's “An enumeration that the problem does not state is C.” I classify pos as R: its least-relation definition supplies the missing semantic condition that a difference is positive. Removing it admits nonpositive differences and changes the relation, rather than just scheduling or enumerating an already constrained set. There is no independent search directive, labelling call, or imposed finite domain here. Treating every invented inductive relation as a C generator would conflict with the R definition and the reference-semantics distinction. This is a potential rule ambiguity, not an amendment I have applied.

Calls to gt/ne are R replacements of the primitive queries; the corresponding named constants remain P. No case or conjunct was moved or omitted. There are no H calls, external mechanisms, or S mechanisms. In particular, definitions of gt/pos/ne are problem-specific mathematical relations, not a reusable interpreter, propagator or scheduler (rules 12 and 19). The empty "'`s_mechanisms` array means none for every P05 program in every configuration; the phase-4 mechanism list is also empty.

## Residuals, reported bindings and representation

The difficult outcome is P05b, not P05c. Stage 1 has both a finite explicit prefix and a finite stored representation of the infinite remaining computation. A cap of twenty derivation blocks does not truncate observe(): the system retains and later acts on all derivations. Classifying only the first twenty integer answers would incorrectly discard that held residual.

The equivalence argument is by hand. Under the specified least-relation semantics, pos(q) is exactly q in the positive integers: the base produces 1 and the recursive case adds 1. Thus `exists d: x=1+d and pos(d)` is exactly integer x>1. Expanding a case and propagating an arithmetic equation preserve that disjunction'"'s solutions. A suspended arithmetic chain ending in pos preserves the unbounded tail. Consequently the entire held state is complete/residual, but reducible to the single comparison x>1, and is not identical to the posed information. This does not infer a finite domain from the observed prefix.

At stage 2, the finished derivations explicitly bind x=2 and x=3. The remaining unfinished derivations include arithmetic work and a pending pick(x). A branch which already binds x=1093 (defaults and wake-back) or x=1410 (depth-first) has not removed that pending constraint: it denotes no solution, since pick is closed-world {1,2,3}. Those bindings are observable, but their branch conditions must accompany them; stripping those conditions would manufacture an unsound answer. The union of the finished branches and the unfinished conditional branches is exactly {2,3}.

I apply SPECIFICATION Outcomes 2's instruction to classify the more explicit valid form, so stage 2 is complete/explicit. The unfinished inconsistent branches, their sizes and their reducibility are recorded as observations. This is an interpretive edge of the “two forms” provision because both forms occur within one derivation-state report. A reading that requires the representation of every retained branch, even redundant empty ones, would instead call the whole stage-2 state complete/residual/reducible. The semantic equivalence is the same. It would be wrong to label the whole residual “inconsistency undetected”: the union has two solutions. A literal reading of the observable-binding sentence as making *every* bound x unconditional would conflict with residual semantics; I preserve its attached pending constraints.

Absys abbreviates some to-do queues as “... N more” even with --full. Therefore the exact deduplicated primitive-relation and unknown-occurrence counts cannot be recovered from every printed state. The JSON gives the available suspended primitive-addition occurrences, exact top-level queue occurrence counts including N, and derivation counts beside the input's one primitive comparison. A recursive pos call has no fixed finite primitive expansion. Queue reactivations may also duplicate an arithmetic relation held as suspended, so the two counts are not summed into a fabricated constraint size. This is a measurement limitation, explicitly marked unavailable where appropriate.

Final behaviour boundary observations for P05b are:

| configuration | stage | finished x values | derivations | printed suspended processes | queued top-level relations |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| absys | 1 | 2–773 | 1288 | 208914 | 248649 |
| absys | 2 | 2, 3 | 731 | 415635 | 497643 |
| absys-depth-first | 1 | 2–998 | 999 | 1992 | 7 |
| absys-depth-first | 2 | 2, 3 | 4 | 1409 | 370 |
| absys-wake-back | 1 | 2–773 | 1288 | 332692 | 1286 |
| absys-wake-back | 2 | 2, 3 | 731 | 663318 | 2549 |

These are retained-state counts, not counts of valid distinct integer solutions. Depth-first keeps all derivations but elaborates one running derivation at a time. No configuration offers a request for further answers, so this is not the execution class “alternatives pending.” All six final P05b stages are budget+suspended. The default and wake-back stage-2 first attempts timed out; their raised-limit attempts reached the budget and determine the final classification. The default's first stage-2 stdout has a UTF-8 harness fault; the final attempt's structured state is available.

## Reachability, timeouts and measurements

For P05a, all configurations finish stage 1 with {1,2,3}, then time out at stage 2 under both limits. There is no observed post-comparison state: none reported, not an empty report and not proof that the mathematical relation is inexpressible. Stage 3's behaviour replay completes only the prelude and stage 1 before timing out again inside stage 2. The repl completion replies and the harness's line-by-line contract establish this. Stage 3 is **not reached**, with semantic and representation fields null. Its raw timeout belongs to the replay, not to ne's own evaluation (AMENDMENTS 3.2). A separately completed restart-count run does not establish that the actual replay completed.

All behaviour P05a records are INVALID because a restart measurement was unavailable for stage 3 attempt 1. Every one of their entries has "'`harness_fault: true`, including their valid stage-1 observations. The corresponding invalid cost/storage records are retained as evidence. The default P05a storage record validates; its mathematical and execution classifications otherwise agree. Missing restart figures and behaviour step figures remain unavailable.

For P05b, all six original cost/storage records time out at both stages with no reported state. These twelve stage differences are in `mode_differences`. The measured whole-text stage-2 attempts expose no assertion-progress information. Although their own stage-1 attempts time out, that is not conclusive evidence locating the stop inside each separate stage-2 attempt. `this_mode.reached` is null there, with an explicit reachability note; its timeout describes the enclosing measurement attempt, not an asserted independent stage-2 failure. This uncertainty is preferable to claiming an unobserved stage was reached or not reached. Behavioural reachability is known.

All six labelled m2 reruns preserve both original measurement records and their meaning. Their twelve final stage classifications match behaviour, including residual equivalence and explicit {2,3}; no differing m2 stage is therefore listed. Cost uses --peak-every 0; storage uses sampled --peak-every 1000. Sampling figures are not exact peaks. These reruns resolve measurement overhead, not mathematical expressibility. P05a and P05c have no m2 reruns. P05c'"'s cost/storage and behaviour classifications agree throughout.

P05c explicitly prints “No derivation survives: the assertions are unsatisfiable.” at stage 2 and accepts stage 3 incrementally without restoring alternatives. The earlier three answers disappear from the surviving set. No manual interventions are recorded; automatic safety reruns and reposing are harness operations.

## Expressibility

All configurations have the same judgement. P05a and P05b are expressible with reformulation: positive integer differences express > over the entire integer domain, and the two directions of > express "'!= on the integer domain already enforced by stage 2 of P05a. This is a declarative equivalence, not a claim of operational completion. P05c is directly expressible. No hidden variants were read, and none were inferred to have passed from these primary runs.

## Totals

| distinct text (first path) | P | C | R | S | H | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| absys/P05a.ab1 | 38 | 0 | 73 | 0 | 0 | 111 |
| absys/P05b.ab1 | 35 | 0 | 44 | 0 | 0 | 79 |
| absys/P05c.ab1 | 44 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 44 |
| total, counted once per distinct text | 117 | 0 | 117 | 0 | 0 | 234 |

Each configuration uses those same 234 tokens; expanding to all configuration copies would give P=351 and R=351, total 702, without changing the distinct-text totals above. Every frozen token index is covered exactly once, and each manifest text is represented.

The 24 behaviour stages comprise 18 complete, 3 none reported, and 3 not reached. Representations are 15 explicit and 3 reducible residuals, with 6 stages having no applicable representation. Execution states are 12 finished, 6 budget+suspended, 3 timeout, and 3 not reached. There are 12 original measurement-stage differences; all 12 m2 stages agree with final behaviour classifications. Supporting mechanisms and late-definition cases: none.

The difficult outcome is P05b, not P05c. Stage 1 has both a finite explicit prefix and a finite stored representation of the infinite remaining computation. A cap of twenty derivation blocks does not truncate observe(): the system retains and later acts on all derivations. Classifying only the first twenty integer answers would incorrectly discard that held residual.

The equivalence argument is by hand. Under the specified least-relation semantics, pos(q) is exactly q in the positive integers: the base produces 1 and the recursive case adds 1. Thus `exists d: x=1+d and pos(d)` is exactly integer x>1. Expanding a case and propagating an arithmetic equation preserve that disjunction'"'s solutions. A suspended arithmetic chain ending in pos preserves the unbounded tail. Consequently the entire held state is complete/residual, but reducible to the single comparison x>1, and is not identical to the posed information. This does not infer a finite domain from the observed prefix.

At stage 2, the finished derivations explicitly bind x=2 and x=3. The remaining unfinished derivations include arithmetic work and a pending pick(x). A branch which already binds x=1093 (defaults and wake-back) or x=1410 (depth-first) has not removed that pending constraint: it denotes no solution, since pick is closed-world {1,2,3}. Those bindings are observable, but their branch conditions must accompany them; stripping those conditions would manufacture an unsound answer. The union of the finished branches and the unfinished conditional branches is exactly {2,3}.

I apply SPECIFICATION Outcomes 2's instruction to classify the more explicit valid form, so stage 2 is complete/explicit. The unfinished inconsistent branches, their sizes and their reducibility are recorded as observations. This is an interpretive edge of the “two forms” provision because both forms occur within one derivation-state report. A reading that requires the representation of every retained branch, even redundant empty ones, would instead call the whole stage-2 state complete/residual/reducible. The semantic equivalence is the same. It would be wrong to label the whole residual “inconsistency undetected”: the union has two solutions. A literal reading of the observable-binding sentence as making *every* bound x unconditional would conflict with residual semantics; I preserve its attached pending constraints.

Absys abbreviates some to-do queues as “... N more” even with --full. Therefore the exact deduplicated primitive-relation and unknown-occurrence counts cannot be recovered from every printed state. The JSON gives the available suspended primitive-addition occurrences, exact top-level queue occurrence counts including N, and derivation counts beside the input's one primitive comparison. A recursive pos call has no fixed finite primitive expansion. Queue reactivations may also duplicate an arithmetic relation held as suspended, so the two counts are not summed into a fabricated constraint size. This is a measurement limitation, explicitly marked unavailable where appropriate.

These are retained-state counts, not counts of valid distinct integer solutions. Depth-first keeps all derivations but elaborates one running derivation at a time. No configuration offers a request for further answers, so this is not the execution class “alternatives pending.” All six final P05b stages are budget+suspended. The default and wake-back stage-2 first attempts timed out; their raised-limit attempts reached the budget and determine the final classification. The default's first stage-2 stdout has a UTF-8 harness fault; the final attempt's structured state is available.

## Reachability, timeouts and measurements

For P05a, all configurations finish stage 1 with {1,2,3}, then time out at stage 2 under both limits. There is no observed post-comparison state: none reported, not an empty report and not proof that the mathematical relation is inexpressible. Stage 3's behaviour replay completes only the prelude and stage 1 before timing out again inside stage 2. The repl completion replies and the harness's line-by-line contract establish this. Stage 3 is **not reached**, with semantic and representation fields null. Its raw timeout belongs to the replay, not to ne's own evaluation (AMENDMENTS 3.2). A separately completed restart-count run does not establish that the actual replay completed.

All behaviour P05a records are INVALID because a restart measurement was unavailable for stage 3 attempt 1. Every one of their entries has "'`harness_fault: true`, including their valid stage-1 observations. The corresponding invalid cost/storage records are retained as evidence. The default P05a storage record validates; its mathematical and execution classifications otherwise agree. Missing restart figures and behaviour step figures remain unavailable.

For P05b, all six original cost/storage records time out at both stages with no reported state. These twelve stage differences are in `mode_differences`. The measured whole-text stage-2 attempts expose no assertion-progress information. Although their own stage-1 attempts time out, that is not conclusive evidence locating the stop inside each separate stage-2 attempt. `this_mode.reached` is null there, with an explicit reachability note; its timeout describes the enclosing measurement attempt, not an asserted independent stage-2 failure. This uncertainty is preferable to claiming an unobserved stage was reached or not reached. Behavioural reachability is known.

All six labelled m2 reruns preserve both original measurement records and their meaning. Their twelve final stage classifications match behaviour, including residual equivalence and explicit {2,3}; no differing m2 stage is therefore listed. Cost uses --peak-every 0; storage uses sampled --peak-every 1000. Sampling figures are not exact peaks. These reruns resolve measurement overhead, not mathematical expressibility. P05a and P05c have no m2 reruns. P05c'"'s cost/storage and behaviour classifications agree throughout.

P05c explicitly prints “No derivation survives: the assertions are unsatisfiable.” at stage 2 and accepts stage 3 incrementally without restoring alternatives. The earlier three answers disappear from the surviving set. No manual interventions are recorded; automatic safety reruns and reposing are harness operations.

## Expressibility

All configurations have the same judgement. P05a and P05b are expressible with reformulation: positive integer differences express > over the entire integer domain, and the two directions of > express "'!= on the integer domain already enforced by stage 2 of P05a. This is a declarative equivalence, not a claim of operational completion. P05c is directly expressible. No hidden variants were read, and none were inferred to have passed from these primary runs.
